# The header-resize motion check opens its 1.8 s window before the hover

## Context

PR #20438's current-head CI went red in [Brain shard 4/10, attempt 1](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42208245847/job/127860217869) at `test/playwright/e2e/grid/HeaderMenuInteractionNL.spec.mjs:355`:

```
expect(observed.samples.some(sample => sample.rects[0]?.width > box.width + 40)).toBe(true)
// received: false
```

The resize arm's native width, worker width and alignment assertions before it passed. The unchanged-head rerun passed. Sophie captured the sighting (two `defect-note` lines, 11:19Z) and routed it to me as the author of #19643, the ticket this spec witnesses.

## The Problem

The arm opens `observeMotion({durationMs: 1800, intervalMs: 32})` before the hover move. It then waits for the resize handle, presses, runs a 30-step move and polls the width. The observer samples a fixed window from the call's arrival in the App worker, and nothing bounds the gesture to that window. The same job's Bridge log shows the race:

| run | `observe_motion` window | next call (post-drop width poll) | gesture past the window's end |
|---|---|---|---|
| attempt 1, red | 11:12:15.511 → 17.350 | 18.388 | 1.04 s |
| attempt 2, green | 11:21:49.294 → 51.109 | 51.233 | 0.12 s |

In both runs the gesture outlived the window. The arm passes only while the width crosses +40 px before the window closes. A slower hover, handle wait or move pushes the crossing past the window. The native and worker polls after it keep their own timeouts and still pass.

A second defect in the same lines: the trace is attached after the assertion, so a red run loses the receipt it needs. The reorder arm (`:143-147`) attaches after its assertion as well.

PR #20404 (#20374) lists this spec as adapter-eligible. After it lands the spec runs in `e2e-engine`, which is a required status context.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/ai/client/ComponentService.mjs#observeMotion` samples `while (Date.now() - start < durationMs)`, with the duration clamped to [100, 8000] ms. No event can end it early.
- The resize arm is `HeaderMenuInteractionNL.spec.mjs:335-356`. The observer starts at `:337`, before `page.mouse.move(x, y)`, the `.neo-resizable-right` wait and `page.mouse.down()`.
- The header keeps its new width after the drop (`:350` asserts the worker width). Any sample taken after the crossing therefore satisfies the assertion. Only a window that closes before the crossing fails.
- Design authority: n/a. The failing spec is the defect; the live-resize behavior it observes stays as asserted.

## The Fix

In the resize arm, open the observer at the gesture: directly after `page.mouse.down()`, before the 30-step move. The hover and the handle wait leave the window. The window keeps its 1.8 s duration and 32 ms interval, and the trace now starts at the original width. In both arms, attach the trace before asserting on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The resize arm's observer starts after `page.mouse.down()`. Its duration, interval and assertion are unchanged.
- [ ] Both arms attach their motion trace before asserting on it.
- [ ] Red on base, as a local control only: with a 1.5 s delay injected before `page.mouse.down()`, the base spec fails at the samples assertion while its geometry assertions pass. The fixed spec passes with the same delay.
- [ ] The complete spec passes `--repeat-each=5 --workers=1` on the fixed head.

## Out of Scope

- `observeMotion`'s fixed-window contract.
- The adapter selection (#20374 / PR #20404).
- Motion assertions in other specs.

## Avoided Traps

- Raising `durationMs` only moves the bet and keeps the race.
- Starting the observer after the native poll sees the growth turns the assertion into a restatement of that poll.
